reason: A selected option must not be ambiguously mapped to canonical AUTHOR_DECISION.status. In particular, approving the act of rejecting a proposal must not produce an APPROVED decision that a downstream Lifecycle gate could misread as affirmative approval.

rules: Every predefined option explicitly declares the canonical AUTHOR_DECISION.status produced if the author selects it.
An affirmative direction/selection uses APPROVED; a reject-all/reject-proposal/retain-current option uses REJECTED when the decision type's downstream semantics treat rejection as non-approval.
The queue must never infer canonical status from option label, display order, provider rank or model preference.
A custom author choice, when allowed, maps to APPROVED as an affirmative author-supplied direction unless a future versioned decision-type contract explicitly defines another mapping.
Lifecycle and other consumers continue to require their existing exact decision_type/status/author_choice semantics and receive no new authority from this clarification.

qualification_delta: predefined APPROVED option maps to canonical APPROVED
predefined REJECTED option maps to canonical REJECTED
reject option cannot accidentally satisfy an APPROVED Lifecycle gate
custom choice mapping remains explicit and no model-selected status is permitted
qualification_effect: NONE until the Author Decision Queue executable subject is qualified. No prior Book qualification is broadened or transferred.
